summary: A monitored quantity with its comparison, in a row whose first or largest tile dominates.
not_for: A category, a name, a date, or a figure on an enter or lookup screen (put it in the heading or the filter bar).

slots.when: Opens the records the figure counts.

rules.rule: The value is a quantity the reader monitors: a count, a rate, an amount.
One comparison: a target, the previous period or a rank.
The row has a dominant tile, by size or by position.
The tiles of a row share one layout.
A tile row belongs to a monitor screen.

labels.label: names the quantity, in the reader's words

evidence.source: S. Few, Common Pitfalls in Dashboard Design (2006)
evidence.says: A figure without context means little; not all data are equally important; equal prominence is failure.
Card dashboards tested well only with high consistency across the cards.
